original.title: Claim leaf encoding admits delimiter collisions
original.evidence: The five fields are joined with unescaped colons before hashing; (claim_id="a:b", advisory_id="c") and (claim_id="a", advisory_id="b:c") with identical remaining fields yield identical preimages.

history.rationale: The exported claim leaf helper concatenates five unrestricted strings with colons. Reachability through every upstream claim producer was not established; confirmation is limited to this public encoding and verifier boundary.

original.evidence: OPCODE_TLOAD = 0x5C + 2 is counted at lines 223-224; EIP-1153 specifies TLOAD=0x5c and TSTORE=0x5d (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1153). bounty_pipeline_orchestrator.py:117,130-145 consumes these results for risk-based receipts.

Counts feed transient-storage risk findings and the orchestrator receipt threshold.

original.title: Concurrent prompt producers and consumers lose FIFO updates
original.evidence: enqueue_prompt and get_next_prompt independently read JSON, modify a list, and write whole file at lines 195 and 206 without locking or atomic replacement.
original.trigger: Two --enqueue processes overlap, or READY consumes while CLI enqueues.
original.impact: Last writer loses newly enqueued prompts or restores consumed prompts; readers can see partial JSON and reset queue.

history.rationale: Queue producers and consumer each read, modify, and overwrite the entire JSON file without a shared lock or atomic update. Two producers can both read Q then leave only Q+A or Q+B; a consumer can race an enqueue and lose or restore a prompt. A partial write can also be treated as an empty queue. No concurrent processes were executed.

guards: Serial operations preserve their simple FIFO behavior.

original.title: Concurrent rate limiter callers reserve the same future slot
original.evidence: _refill resets _last_refill=now even when it was a future reservation; every deficit caller then sets tokens=0 and last_refill=clock()+wait_s.
original.trigger: Several threads acquire while the bucket is empty before the first waiting caller wakes.
original.impact: They all receive approximately the same wait and dispatch together, violating the intended rate bound and increasing upstream throttling.

history.rationale: A deficit caller stores a future refill time; the next caller at the same clock value resets it to now, leaving zero tokens and reserving the same wait. For a depleted 15-RPM bucket, multiple callers each receive 4 seconds instead of successive slots. query sleeps after the lock is released. The thread lock prevents data races but not duplicate future reservations.

source_checks.observation: _refill resets future _last_refill and deficit calculation does not accumulate pending debt.
Rate-limiter result is slept independently before network dispatch.
Existing deterministic test covers only the first deficit caller.

guards: threading.Lock serializes calculation but releases before sleep.
Quota is a daily budget and is not an inter-request rate constraint.

original.title: A contender removes an active installer lock after approximately one second
original.evidence: acquire_lock unconditionally rm -rf removes LOCK_DIR after 200 failed mkdir attempts with sleep 0.005; no owner PID, liveness, or ownership check exists. release_lock also deletes whichever lock currently exists.
original.trigger: Two installs/uninstalls overlap and the first takes more than the fixed wait interval.
original.impact: Both processes can enter the critical section and race on global skills, configuration and workspace rules.

history.rationale: A competing installer deletes the shared lock directory after more than 200 failed mkdir attempts separated by 5ms sleeps, regardless of owner liveness. A still-running owner can therefore overlap a new owner; either release may remove the replacement lock. The nominal wait is about one second plus command overhead, not a stale-owner proof.

source_checks.observation: Acquisition forcibly removes an existing lock after a retry count and release unconditionally removes the path.
The lock and EXIT trap cover the installation body.
Normal completion also removes the lock without ownership validation.

guards: mkdir provides atomic initial acquisition only.
Neither a PID/nonce nor an ownership/inode check protects eviction or release.
